newsitem.title: CHILE: Castro attacks privatization, visits Allende tomb.
newsitem.headline: Castro attacks privatization, visits Allende tomb.

text.p: Cuban President Fidel Castro visited the tomb of Chile's late Marxist president Salvador Allende on Sunday and later spoke passionately in defence of the socialist ideals that both of them upheld.
At the Sixth Ibero-American Summit, Castro also flatly rejected a proposal by Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar that he open the way to reforms to Cuba's one-party political system.

Castro shook up the summit with a speech lashing out at privatisation, U.S. mass media and foreign capital, showing his socialist zeal undimmed while the rest of the region turns to free-market economics.

"As long as everything is privatised at any price and the state sells off the wealth that past generations accumulated with great sacrifice ... what future awaits us?" said Castro, dressed in a blue civilian suit instead of his usual battle fatigues.
He excoriated "foreign capital and transnationals (that) take over the centres of production of the most strategic goods and services" and U.S. mass media that "dismember our culture."

Castro made the speech sitting at the same table as such presidents as Peru's Alberto Fujimori and Argentina's Carlos Menem, who have privatised dozens of state companies between them and courted foreign investment.
Spanish government sources travelling with Aznar said later that at a lunch between the two leaders, Castro rejected Aznar's proposal that Cuba start political reforms.
Aznar told Castro that he would persuade the European Union to help Cuba if "you're willing to make a move and open your country to democracy," the sources said.

"I'm not willing to make a move," Castro told Aznar, according to the sources. The two leaders swapped ties in a sign of friendship. Castro walked out of the lunch with the dapper Aznar's silk Hermes tie, they said.
Castro, making his first visit to Chile since Allende's presidency in 1971, earlier visited the late socialist's tomb in a quiet, emotional encounter in Santiago's General Cemetery.
He stood silently for a few moments at the stone tomb emblazoned with Allende's name and greeted Allende's daughter Isabel and Chilean leftist politicians.

Allende died in a 1973 coup as military jets bombed the presidential palace. His personal physician later said he saw Allende commit suicide with a submachine gun given to him by Castro, but some ex-confidants say he was murdered.
The leaders of 19 Latin American nations plus Spain and Portugal were attending the summit, which ends Monday.
